description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative. Choose your own model and sandbox.
readmeExcerpt:
# Rakazo [English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](./README.ja.md) Rakazo is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot. Persistent AI teammates with their own memory, routines, apps, and computer. Run it on your own machine, with your own model. Use it on the [web](https://app.rakazo.com), [desktop](https://rakazo.com/download/), [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099), and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app). It is also an alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Claude Duet. Learn more at [rakazo.com](https://rakazo.com). ## Features - Routines - Memory - Computer and browser use - Private or shared team computers - Sandboxes in Docker, the cloud, or on your own machine - Group chats - Delegation and subagents - Builds dashboards and docs you can share by link - Voice chat and calls - Any model, with your own keys - Thousands of app integrations, plus MCP
### Every bot gets a computer A browser, terminal, files, and a full desktop. Watch it work, take control to sign in, and hand it back. ### Bots that work together Put bots in a group and @mention them. They split the work, check each other, and report back.
### Routines Run a bot on a schedule, from an email, or from a webhook, and see every run. ### Pages Bots build live dashboards and documents you can open full screen, share, and ask about.
### Connected apps Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and thousands more, plus your own MCP servers and OpenAPI tools. ### On every device Web, desktop, iPhone, iPad, and Android, all talking to the same server.
## Quick start (published images) You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install. ```bash mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo && curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh && bash install-images.sh ``` The installer downloads the Compose files, creates `.env` with random secrets, and starts Rakazo. It preserves an existing `.env` when rerun. Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173), create an account, and connect a model. Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `novita`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, `boxd`, `instabox`, or `railway` with the matching API key. Default image tag is `edge` (main builds, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). Details and tags: [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout). On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap script URL — see [Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads). For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md). ## Run on a server Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser. ```bash bash install-images.sh --prepare-only # edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain bash install-images.sh ``` Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; [docs/self-host-production.md](./docs/self-host-production.md#public-single-vm-deployment) covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose **Existing instance** and enter the `https://` address. Or [deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/new/template/rakazo-template); see the [Railway setup guide](./infra/railway/README.md). ## Local development (source checkout) You need Node.js 24.15.0 or newer in the 24.x line, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 12; and Docker. Node.js 25.x is not supported. ```bash git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git cd rakazo cp .env.example .env ``` Set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD` to two values from `openssl rand -hex 16`, then put them in `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. The app connects as its own `rakazo_app` login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner ([database roles](docs/self-host-configuration.md#database-roles)). Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET` to independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated `SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`. You can also set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or connect a supported model provider during onboarding. For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set `SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true` in `.env`. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically; `DOCKER_HOST` or `DOCKER_SOCKET` can override it for another Docker runtime. Managed app catalogs are optional. Set `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` for Composio, or the `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID`, `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID` trio for Pipedream Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server or OpenAPI JSON document from **Integrations** without enabling either managed catalog. Connector credentials are encrypted on the server and are never returned by the API. Paid data services (map places, search results, work emails, profiles, SEO data) are optional too. Set `PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg` and `PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY` to an org-scoped [Treg](https://treg.to) token, and bots can find and call them on the deployment's account. When model credits are on, each call is charged to the organization's credits at the provider's cost plus 20%. ```bash pnpm install pnpm sandbox:build pnpm dev ``` `pnpm dev` uses the Postgres in `DATABASE_URL` when it accepts a connection. Otherwise it starts a local `rakazo-dev-postgres` container with Docker, and every checkout reuses that one. It applies migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible, so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set `WEB_PORT` and `API_PORT` to choose ports yourself. To try a checkout from your phone or another computer, install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) on each device and set `RAKAZO_DEV_TAILNET=1` in `.env`. `pnpm dev` then serves the web app over HTTPS at `https://..ts.net:`, reachable only from devices on your tailnet, and stops serving it when you quit. Sign in at that URL on every device, including the one running it. The first run may ask you to turn on HTTPS certificates for your tailnet. To keep keys in a secrets manager instead of `.env`, set `RAKAZO_DEV_RUN_WITH` to the command that runs another with your secrets added, for example `op run --env-file=dev.env --` or `infisical run --env=dev --projectId= --`. `pnpm dev` then starts inside it, and the values it adds win over `.env`. To run Postgres from the Compose file instead, start it with the `postgres-host` overlay, which publishes loopback `127.0.0.1:5433`, and point `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` at it: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \ up postgres -d ``` Use a URI-safe `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (`openssl rand -hex 16`). An existing `pgdata` volume keeps the user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in `.env`, or change them in place with `ALTER ROLE` / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is disposable); `docker compose down -v` deletes all Postgres state. Open the printed URL ([http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173) by default), create an account, connect a model, and create your first bot. For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md), [production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md), [backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md), and [upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md). To use CreateOS, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos` and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY`. Optional `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL`, `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE`, and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS` default to `https://api.sb.createos.sh`, `s-2vcpu-2gb`, and `desktop:1`. To use Railway computers, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway`, `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN` and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment. Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a personal account token. The live screen and desktop require `PRIVATE` networking so Railway's public domain can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes, separate from the app and database. Recreate existing `ISOLATED` computers before use. The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox. Railway sandbox usage is metered. New computers start in Railway's default region. Set `RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION` (for example `asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start. Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set `RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES` to change this limit. ## Desktop and mobile The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app. With the development stack running, launch Electron with: ```bash pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev ``` On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing server. **This computer** can run without Docker on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or later when the build includes a server bundle. Fresh setups use this path: the app downloads the server and computer runtime as needed. Existing Docker setups are offered a move while Docker is running; choosing **Keep Docker** leaves them on Docker. Other builds and platforms use Docker Compose to install and start the published images (the same files as `infra/compose/install-images.sh`) under the app's data directory. This path needs Docker Desktop, OrbStack, or Docker Engine. Without one, setup offers the Docker Desktop download, opens an installed Docker app that is not running, and continues on its own once Docker answers. Installed builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull `edge`. Developers running `pnpm dev` should pick **Existing instance** with `http://127.0.0.1:5173` ins

releases.name: Rakazo v0.11.0
releases.body:
### Security

- Updated third-party dependencies with known vulnerabilities, including the HTTP client used by model, mail and scraping connections, the mail sender, and XML and Markdown parsers.
- The development launcher's database cleanup accepts only database names it generated and quotes them, so forged database metadata can no longer inject SQL or point the cleanup at another folder. This affects source checkouts only.

### Added

- On Apple silicon Macs running macOS 26 or newer, the desktop app's **This computer** runs without Docker. The app downloads what it needs the first time you pick it, and each bot's computer runs as its own small VM with a firewall that lets it reach the internet but not your Mac or local network. If you already run This computer on Docker, the app asks once whether to move your bots and data; Docker is stopped, not removed. Intel Macs, older macOS, Linux and Windows keep using Docker ([This computer on a Mac without Docker](docs/desktop-mac-without-docker.md)).
- Message your bots from Microsoft Teams direct messages after linking your Teams account ([messaging apps](docs/messaging-apps.md)).
- Routines can watch a public HTTPS address and run on

releases.name: Rakazo v0.10.0
releases.body:
### Security

- Updated the IP-address parser to fix a regular-expression denial of service affecting address parsing in rate limiting and proxy connections.
- Failed MCP responses now have a total size limit even when they use an event stream, preventing oversized error responses from being buffered without a bound.

### Added

- In the desktop app's **This computer** mode, bots can see and use Mac and Windows apps when **Let bots use this computer** is enabled. Screen access is limited to owner-started chats and asks for approval on the first use of each app in a Space ([computer](docs/computer.md)).
- See subscription allowances, reset times and remaining credits in the account menu and Settings > Usage, with the same breakdown on the mobile account screen.
- Voice connections can reuse a supported model sign-in for speech and transcription instead of requiring another key ([voice and calls](docs/voice-and-calls.md)).
- Added another optional remote computer adapter with suspend and resume support ([computer providers](docs/self-host-sandbox-providers.md#instabox-computers)).
- Mobile now offers French, Hebrew, Hindi, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish; Hebrew uses a righ

releases.name: Rakazo v0.9.0
releases.body:
### Security

- Mobile discards sign-ins that finish after a server change, preventing the previous server's session credentials from reaching the new server. Offline sign-out now retries session revocation when connectivity returns; Android also suppresses bot notifications while signed out. On iOS, old notification previews can still appear until revocation reaches the server.
- Credentials passed in local MCP server launch arguments are hidden from tool output, errors and run history, including authorization flags, numeric secret values and passwords in URLs.
- Incus computers explicitly start as an unprivileged user, including custom images without a declared user. Remote command working directories stay within the bot workspace, and team-chat attachment names are sanitized before entering bot context.
- Computer helpers no longer load Python code from the bot-writable home directory or inherit the control token when starting commands, protecting saved logins and payment details.
- The desktop computer viewer can no longer read the host clipboard. Copying from the bot's computer to the host clipboard is disabled; pasting into it remains available.
- Calls ask for voice consent

releases.name: Rakazo for Android 1.0.14 (33)
releases.body: Install rakazo.apk on your Android phone. It updates itself over the air.

releases.name: Rakazo v0.8.0
releases.body:
### Added

- On iPhone and iPad, an image pasted into a chat's message field is added as an attachment, as on web. Text copied with it still goes into the field. This needs the new app build.
- On iPhone and iPad, Rakazo appears in the share sheet. Share a link, text, photos or files from any app, pick a bot, and it lands in that bot's message field as a draft. This needs the new app build.
- More keyboard shortcuts on web and desktop: start a group chat, connect apps, open the chat's details panel, jump to the message box and dictate. Cmd/Ctrl+/ lists every shortcut, as do **Keyboard shortcuts** in the command menu and **Help** in the desktop app.
- Cmd/Ctrl+F in the desktop app finds text in the open chat, highlighting every match and stepping through them. Searching bots moves to Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F.
- The web app is fully translated into Turkish. Before, large parts of it fell back to English.

Rakazo is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot.

Persistent AI teammates with their own memory, routines, apps, and computer. Run it on your own machine, with your own model.

Use it on the web, desktop, iPhone, and Android.

It is also an alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Claude Duet.

Learn more at rakazo.com.

Features

  • Memory
  • Computer and browser use
  • Private or shared team computers

  • Delegation and subagents
  • Builds dashboards and docs you can share by link

  • Thousands of app integrations, plus MCP

Bots that work together

Put bots in a group and @mention them. They split the work, check each other, and report back.

Routines

Run a bot on a schedule, from an email, or from a webhook, and see every run.

Pages

Connected apps

Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and thousands more, plus your own MCP servers and OpenAPI tools.

On every device

Web, desktop, iPhone, iPad, and Android, all talking to the same server.

Quick start (published images)

You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install.

mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo &&
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh &&
bash install-images.sh

Open http://127.0.0.1:5173, create an account, and connect a model. Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: e2b, novita, daytona, createos, boat, boxd, instabox, or railway with the matching API key.

Default image tag is edge (main builds, linux/amd64 + linux/arm64). Details and tags: self-hosting guide.

On restricted networks, override the installer download base (RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE), skip existing Compose files (--local / RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING), or mirror the bootstrap script URL — see Restricted networks / mirror downloads.

For an agent-assisted install, use SETUP_PROMPT.md.

Run on a server

Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser.

bash install-images.sh --prepare-only
# edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain
bash install-images.sh

Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; docs/self-host-production.md covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose Existing instance and enter the https:// address.

Or deploy on Railway; see the Railway setup guide.

Local development (source checkout)

You need Node.js 24.15.0 or newer in the 24.x line, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 12; and Docker. Node.js 25.x is not supported.

git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git
cd rakazo
cp .env.example .env

The app connects as its own rakazo_app login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner (database roles). Set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY, and SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET to independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN. You can also set OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or connect a supported model provider during onboarding.

For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true in .env. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically; DOCKER_HOST or DOCKER_SOCKET can override it for another Docker runtime.

Managed app catalogs are optional. Set COMPOSIO_API_KEY for Composio, or the PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID, PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET, and PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID trio for Pipedream Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server or OpenAPI JSON document from Integrations without enabling either managed catalog. Connector credentials are encrypted on the server and are never returned by the API.

Set PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg and PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY to an org-scoped Treg token, and bots can find and call them on the deployment's account. When model credits are on, each call is charged to the organization's credits at the provider's cost plus 20%.

pnpm install
pnpm sandbox:build
pnpm dev

It applies migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible, so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set WEB_PORT and API_PORT to choose ports yourself.

docker compose --env-file .env \
  -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \
  -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \
  up postgres -d

Use a URI-safe POSTGRES_PASSWORD (openssl rand -hex 16). An existing pgdata volume keeps the user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in .env, or change them in place with ALTER ROLE / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is disposable); docker compose down -v deletes all Postgres state.

Open the printed URL (http://127.0.0.1:5173 by default), create an account, connect a model, and create your first bot.

For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the self-hosting guide, production deployment, backup and restore, and upgrading.

To use CreateOS, set SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos and CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY. Optional CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL, CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE, and CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS default to https://api.sb.createos.sh, s-2vcpu-2gb, and desktop:1.

To use Railway computers, set SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway, RAILWAY_API_TOKEN and RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment. Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a personal account token. The live screen and desktop require PRIVATE networking so Railway's public domain can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes, separate from the app and database. Recreate existing ISOLATED computers before use. The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox. Railway sandbox usage is metered. New computers start in Railway's default region. Set RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION (for example asia-southeast1-eqsg3a) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start. Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES to change this limit.

Desktop and mobile

The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app.

With the development stack running, launch Electron with:

pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev

On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing server. This computer can run without Docker on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or later when the build includes a server bundle. Fresh setups use this path: the app downloads the server and computer runtime as needed. Existing Docker setups are offered a move while Docker is running; choosing Keep Docker leaves them on Docker.

Other builds and platforms use Docker Compose to install and start the published images (the same files as infra/compose/install-images.sh) under the app's data directory. This path needs Docker Desktop, OrbStack, or Docker Engine. Without one, setup offers the Docker Desktop download, opens an installed Docker app that is not running, and continues on its own once Docker answers. Installed builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull edge. Developers running pnpm dev should pick Existing instance with http://127.0.0.1:5173 instead. Public servers must use HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback and private LAN addresses (not link-local). The app verifies Rakazo's health endpoint before saving, and later launches go straight to that instance. The Docker stack keeps running after the app quits; the Docker-free server stops with the app. Stop Local Stack in the application menu stops the managed stack without quitting.

On Linux the desktop app ships as an AppImage, which needs FUSE 2 (libfuse.so.2). Distributions that only include FUSE 3, such as Fedora Silverblue or Ubuntu 24.04, show dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2. Install the FUSE 2 library (fuse-libs on Fedora, libfuse2t64 on Ubuntu 24.04, libfuse2 on older Ubuntu and Debian), or run the AppImage without FUSE:

chmod +x Rakazo-*.AppImage
./Rakazo-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run

The Docker path of This computer looks for the docker CLI and does not detect Podman. To try another Docker-compatible CLI that supports the compose commands, set RAKAZO_DOCKER_BINARY to its path before starting the app.

Use Change Rakazo Server… in the application menu to reconnect. Closing that window without saving returns to the previous instance. For development automation, set RAKAZO_WEB_URL to point the shell somewhere else without changing the saved instance, or RAKAZO_FORCE_SETUP=1 to run setup again.

Mobile build and release instructions live in docs/mobile-release.md.

UI language

The web (and Electron-hosted) UI supports English, Deutsch, 한국어, Türkçe, हिन्दी, Português (Brasil), 简体中文, 繁體中文, Español, Русский, Français, עברית, Nederlands, 日本語, and Polski under Settings → Language. The Expo app ships the same 15 languages under Account → Language. A device language or EXPO_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_UI_LOCALE still selects the starting catalog before a saved choice. Native Electron setup and menus also support the web UI's languages, following the saved app choice or, on first launch, the system language. The marketing homepage (apps/www) offers all 15 languages through footer links, including /zh/ and /zh-tw/; other marketing pages remain primarily English.

Development

apps/       web, api, worker, desktop, mobile, and public website
packages/   domain, contracts, persistence, adapters, UI, and test tooling
infra/      local services and computer images
docs/       architecture, operations, and release guides

Common checks:

pnpm lint
pnpm check
pnpm test
pnpm test:integration
pnpm test:e2e

See CONTRIBUTING.md for the development workflow and test matrix.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source desktop and self-hosted platform for running local and remote Docker-based AI sandboxes for bots.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Rakazo provides a unified platform to create, run, and manage AI bots in secure Docker sandboxes either locally or on remote servers like Railway and CreateOS. It uses a desktop app (Electron) or a web interface to connect a model provider and orchestrate agent workspaces without complex local setups. The backend relies on Node.js and PostgreSQL with row-level security for robust multi-tenant capabilities, and it uses Compose files to manage container lifecycles natively. It also features a supervisor for host-side Docker control and supports managed app catalogs like Composio and Pipedream for extended agent integrations.
keyFeatures: Cross-platform Client: Connects to local Docker engines or remote VPS instances through Electron desktop or Expo mobile apps.
Containerized Sandboxing: Creates secure and portable environments for AI bots with automatic workspace persistence.
Multi-provider Remote Support: Provisions sandboxes on cloud platforms like Railway, CreateOS, or E2B with simple API keys.
Integrated Identity Management: Secures tenant data in PostgreSQL using row-level security and independent encryption keys.
Agent Extension Catalogs: Connects directly with Composio and Pipedream Connect, or custom OpenAPI and MCP endpoints.
Offline-capable Local Mode: Bootstraps local environments over loopback networks without requiring public internet exposure.
